clue.text: Tedious chap isn't complicated — just crude

indicators.note: complicated means made tangled or involved, so the letters of the three preceding words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A dull man is far from intricate; he is simply coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' looks like part of the description of the chap, but it signals that TEDIOUS, CHAP and ISNT (the apostrophe adds no letter) are rearranged together; 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude is rough and lacking refinement, which is the sense of naive or unworldly here.

clue.text: Unqualified to speak

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or absolute, as in total nonsense without qualification; as a verb it means to say something out loud.

clue.text: New Testament revelation

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of testament are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: Something revealed in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as the Bible's second part, but 'New' is the anagram signal working on TESTAMENT alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement can be a disclosure or declaration, the making known of something previously unsaid.

clue.text: Look like a lord

explanation.surface: Appear to be a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To look closely or squint at something is one sense; a member of the nobility, such as a baron or earl, is the other.

clue.text: Uplift at home has religious point

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
the pointed top of a church steeple

explanation.surface: Being at home with a church steeple raises the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift is to fill with encouragement or spiritual elevation, the effect of stirring someone.

clue.text: Sour at first, then permitted to be a little sweet

parts.note: tart means sharp or acidic in taste
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Something tastes acidic at first, but is then allowed to become mildly sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little sweet' reads as a mild flavour, but it defines a small pastry dessert; 'at first, then' just sets the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pastry case holding fruit or jam is literally a little sweet dish.

clue.text: Hastily cobbled together one pointless clue. Sorry!

indicators.note: cobbled together means roughly assembled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: pointless means without a point; E (east) is a compass point and is dropped from the word clue

explanation.surface: A setter apologises for a clue thrown together carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' takes E, the compass point, out of CLUE to leave CLU; 'cobbled together' then rearranges I, CLU and SORRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a quick, superficial manner without care is doing it in haste.

clue.text: Old Testament character bringing African witchcraft into Tobago?

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: TT is the international code for Trinidad and Tobago; the question mark admits it covers more than Tobago
obi (or obeah) is a form of sorcery of West African origin practised in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A biblical figure brings West African magic to a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for Trinidad and Tobago, hence the question mark. Tobit is the hero of a book of the Apocrypha, which some Bibles print with the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The pious Israelite of the Book of Tobit, blinded and later healed, is a figure from scripture before Christ.

clue.text: Check what I have, to reach a conclusion

parts.note: to check is to hold back or deter
what I have is mine

explanation.surface: Someone inspects their own belongings in order to settle a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like inspecting, but it means restrain; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide or settle a matter after thought is to arrive at a final judgement.

clue.text: Ill-starred businessmen

indicators.note: ill here means badly, so the letters of starred are put into a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Unlucky merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-starred' reads as one word meaning unlucky, but 'Ill' is the anagram signal and 'starred' its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers who buy and sell goods are people engaged in commerce.

clue.text: Not an uncommon coin if it's Welsh

definitions.text: Not an uncommon coin if it's Welsh

parts.words: Not an uncommon coin if it's Welsh
parts.note: read literally it suggests a scarce piece of money, but the Welsh version of this word is a cheese-on-toast dish, not currency

explanation.surface: A Welsh coin is not, after all, a scarce one.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as RARE (uncommon) and BIT (coin, as in a threepenny bit, an old British coin), but with Welsh in front it is cheese melted on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of seasoned melted cheese on toast, so with Welsh it names food rather than money.

clue.text: Air — or wind

explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish or Irish dance tune is a kind of melody; to coil a line or fishing tackle round a spool is to wind.

clue.text: Hoarding coverage? This could be his occupation

definitions.text: Hoarding coverage? This could be his occupation

parts.words: Hoarding coverage? This could be his occupation
parts.note: a hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board; the man whose job is pasting notices over it gives it its coverage

explanation.surface: A job description for the person who covers advertising boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' tempts as stockpiling, but in Britain a hoarding is a big roadside billboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to paste advertising sheets on walls and boards has that as his trade.

clue.text: Quietly associate with a priest

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to relate is to connect or associate

explanation.surface: Keep a low profile while mixing with a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other senior churchman is a high-ranking member of the clergy.

clue.text: Unusual developments, men — phone a doctor!

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something odd is happening, chaps; call a GP!
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as the medic to phone, but it is a verb meaning tamper with, rearranging MEN and PHONE into PHENOMEN, with A added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable occurrences or observable events, especially strange ones, are what the word names.

clue.text: A relation up the creek is one who repels

indicators.note: up the creek means in trouble or in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A family member in difficulty turns people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the creek' is slang for in trouble and signals the anagram of A RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who estranges or drives others away causes hostility and distance.

clue.text: Slip on spilt oil in Middle East port

parts.note: to slip is to trip

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters of oil are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing on a pool of oil in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges OIL into OLI; 'on' and 'in' are links. The city meant is the Lebanese one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lebanese city on the Mediterranean is a seaport in the Levant.

clue.text: Foul, undoubtedly — turn on us and boo eleven!

indicators.note: turn means change round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and also a word for a team of eleven

explanation.surface: Fans are nasty, certainly: they round on the team and jeer it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn on us' reads as attacking, but 'turn' signals the rearrangement of ON US, BOO and XI; 'undoubtedly' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty, offensive or repellent is objectionable in the extreme.

clue.text: Initiations when guards have been decapitated!

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the word for guards loses its first letter

parts.note: sentries are soldiers keeping guard

explanation.surface: Beheadings of soldiers on watch are a gruesome way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have been decapitated' removes the first letter from SENTRIES; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissions or beginnings, the act of going in, are what initiations amount to.

clue.text: This helps one to hear small rumble of satisfaction, and it's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces are read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a purr is the contented rumbling sound of a cat
it's here is it is, so it supplies the letters and 's is the verb

explanation.surface: A satisfied murmur goes up as someone strains to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the purr and the 'it' upwards together, giving TIRRUP after S. The definition points to the tiny bone of the middle ear, not the riding gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, a small bone in the middle ear, is so called from its shape and passes sound vibrations inward.

clue.text: An older academic, accomplished, with desire to be retained

indicators.note: to be retained means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: done means accomplished or finished
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A senior scholar who has achieved much wants to keep her post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accomplished' looks like praise of the academic, but it gives DONE, which holds YEN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior and most respected woman in a field is the most experienced of its members.

clue.text: Old fuel pollution down in the dumps

indicators.note: pollution suggests contamination and corruption, so the letters of old fuel are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Fumes from stale petrol leave people miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pollution' is a noun but signals the rearrangement of OLD FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps is being gloomy and sorrowful.

clue.text: Boys silent — flummoxed, to all intents and purposes

indicators.note: flummoxed means confused, so the letters of boys silent are mixed up

explanation.surface: Puzzled lads fall quiet, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flummoxed' reads as describing the quiet boys, but it signals the anagram of BOYS SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently, or seemingly, is how a thing appears on the face of it.

clue.text: Tribute to a good man

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: Honouring a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a dedication, but 'Tribute' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses in honour of someone is a gesture of respect.

clue.text: A number backing the coalition

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the number word is reversed

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: A figure supporting the governing alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for the coalition, but it reverses SIX to XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War was known by this name.

clue.text: Spots, it's said, in specific spots

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: spots as a verb means sees or catches sight of, sights

explanation.surface: Blemishes, it is claimed, appear in particular places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' first tempts as the definition, but here it is the verb sights, and its sound gives the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations set aside for a particular purpose, like building plots, are particular places.

clue.text: Colours fade

explanation.surface: Paint loses its brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its banner; to fade is to weaken or droop with tiredness.

clue.text: Yet he still plays Shylock?

parts.note: the word splits as a former player who has quit the stage, yet Shylock's role in The Merchant of Venice is to demand his debt, so in that sense the name still fits

explanation.surface: A retired performer somehow still takes the role of Shakespeare's moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as ex-actor, one who no longer acts, but it is also one who exacts payment, as Shylock does with his pound of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: One who demands money or obedience, such as an extortionate creditor, is someone who insists on payment.

clue.text: Disagree about nuclear aftermath

explanation.surface: Arguing over the consequences of an atomic blast.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel is to fall out; radioactive dust settling after a bomb is the other sense.

clue.text: They're studying humanity, poor things — also worrying about time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
worrying means agitated and troubled, so the letters of poor things and also are shaken up

explanation.surface: Scholars of mankind fret over the passing hours, unfortunate creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' rearranges POOR THINGS and ALSO, and 'about' places that around T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists of mankind examine human societies, cultures and development.
